title: Vandals
capsule: The Vandals were a Germanic people who migrated from the Baltic region southward through Gaul and Iberia before crossing into North Africa in 429 under King Gaiseric, who captured Carthage in 439 and established a kingdom that lasted until 534. Gaiseric transformed the Vandals into a naval power that raided the western Mediterranean coastlines, sacking Rome itself in 455 in a fortnight-long plundering. The Byzantine general Belisarius destroyed the kingdom in the Vandalic War (533–534), capturing King Gelimer and dispersing the Vandal population through the eastern empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Vandal kingdom's North African core (roughly modern Tunisia and eastern Algeria) is well documented in late Roman and Byzantine sources; the earlier migration-period territorial footprint in Gaul and Hispania is far less precisely bounded.
